name: Aristolochic acid (Aristolochia herbs)
short: Reviews describe aristolochic acid as kidney-toxic and cancer-causing: a rapidly progressive kidney disease, often ending in kidney failure, and urinary tract cancer in almost half of those patients.
text: Aristolochic acid is a toxin found in plants of the genus Aristolochia, and reviews describe it as nephrotoxic and carcinogenic. A review of the evidence describes a rapidly progressive kidney disease (aristolochic acid nephropathy) first reported in young Belgian women who followed a slimming regimen containing Chinese herbs, with early severe anaemia and extensive scarring of the kidney; cancer of the lining of the upper urinary tract later developed in almost half of those patients, and the review says that similar cases have been observed throughout the world and that the substance was withdrawn in several countries. A second review states that progression to end-stage kidney disease is rapid, that most patients go on to need dialysis or a kidney transplant, and that the nephropathy is associated with a 40-45% prevalence of urothelial cancers; these proportions refer to patients who already have the nephropathy, not to everyone exposed. In a systematic review and meta-analysis of epidemiological studies, aristolochic acid exposure was associated with upper urinary tract urothelial cancer (pooled odds ratio 5.97, 95% CI 2.78 to 12.84), the risk of end-stage kidney disease rose with cumulative exposure, and the authors noted that exposure can also occur when Aristolochia plants are inadvertently mixed with harvested food crops. No interaction data were found in the cited sources.
